assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and its conversion into incretin therapies has changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefits; the arc from hormone biology to widely used drugs is clear, original and of very large impact on patients.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established the physiology and biology of GLP-1 and its actions; Knudsen led the pharmaceutical development of long-acting analogues. Mojsov's contribution to peptide identification and characterisation is a credit question I cannot resolve from the supplied text; a three-person configuration remains workable.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation, large randomized outcome trials and broad clinical adoption; recognition is timely and in no sense premature.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen is contested and I have not independently verified the historical record.
Whether the committee prefers basic physiology or drug development emphasis is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed at tumour antigens opened a new therapeutic modality, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies; the concept is original and the clinical impact is clear.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June developed the chimeric receptor designs with costimulation and clinical translation; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early clinical gene-engineered T-cell therapy. The three names give a coherent configuration, though others (e.g. Eshhar, Kuwana) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long follow-up in haematological cancers; solid-tumour efficacy, toxicity and cost remain limits but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Foundational chimeric-receptor credit outside the supplied names may be material.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated channels used as genetically targeted tools transformed causal dissection of neural circuits, including the motor and sensory circuits I know best; the method is widely adopted and reached beyond neuroscience.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterised channelrhodopsin, with Bamberg in the same line; Deisseroth established its neuronal application and the technology; Boyden and Miesenboeck contributed to early neuronal control. The six-name credit is crowded, and a three-person prize forces difficult exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent use and replication; maturity is high, though clinical translation is still early.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely contested among six credited people.
I am a user of related tools, so I note my field closeness and have tried not to let it inflate the rank.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic from the ER to the nucleus, with implications for secretory biology, metabolic disease, neurodegeneration and cancer; the discovery is conceptually clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori identified the central Ire1-Hac1/XBP1 signalling and ER-to-nucleus communication; a two-person configuration is a clean fit. Other contributors to branches of the pathway (e.g. Ron, Harding) are outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is thoroughly confirmed over many years in many systems; direct clinical translation is still developing.
uncertainties: Clinical consequences are less established than the basic mechanism.
Credit for the PERK and ATF6 branches lies outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides corrected SMN2 splicing and yielded nusinersen, a disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, a motor neuron disease where there had been no effective treatment; a direct bench-to-bedside success with a new drug class.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and regulatory elements; Bennett led the antisense platform and drug development at Ionis. This pair is a natural configuration; the role of the clinical trial leaders is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term outcome data; broad recognition is timely. Contemporary gene therapy and small molecules complicate the narrative but do not erase it.
uncertainties: Contribution of the Adrian Krainer/Ionis collaboration versus others (e.g. Gideon Dreyfuss, Ravindra Singh) is not covered in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is the best-established cellular model of activity-dependent synaptic plasticity and has framed memory research for fifty years; its conceptual importance is very high.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo discovered LTP in the hippocampus in 1973; Collingridge identified the NMDA-receptor dependence, a decisive mechanistic step. Morris tied it to spatial learning but is the fourth name. This three-person set follows the discovery and mechanism line.
assessment.maturity: Very mature; however, the causal link between LTP and memory remains debated, and the practical medical impact is indirect.
uncertainties: Whether the causal link to memory formation is considered sufficiently settled.
Omission of Morris, and of Nicoll and Malenka, who are outside this credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and the discovery of a conserved nutrient and growth regulatory network that influences metabolism, ageing, cancer and immunity; the concept is original and widely consequential.
assessment.attribution: Hall's discovery of TOR in yeast is the decisive step; Sabatini and Schreiber contributed mammalian mTOR identification and mechanistic work, but I would propose Hall alone as the clearest core, noting a larger configuration is possible.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and clinically relevant through rapalogs, though broad therapeutic benefit has been selective.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would add mTOR identification credit (Sabatini, Schreiber).
Contested conduct questions around one candidate are not something I can evaluate from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cloning of leptin and demonstration that a circulating adipose-derived hormone regulates body weight established the endocrine basis of appetite control and opened the field of energy-balance neuroscience, linking to hypothalamic circuits.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit lists only Friedman. The discovery was also built on Coleman's parabiosis work and the Zhang et al. cloning team, and downstream receptor work involved others not in this candidate; the single-name configuration is a risk.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in human leptin deficiency, where replacement therapy is effective, though the broader obesity application was limited; GLP-1 therapy has since overshadowed it clinically.
uncertainties: Credit beyond the supplied single name (Coleman, Chua, Tartaglia) is not available here.
Clinical impact is narrow compared with the conceptual impact.
